clue.text: Encouragement given for so long and much appreciated

definitions.meaning: shouts of support from a crowd urging someone on
an informal British way of saying goodbye
an informal British way of saying thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a friend for support offered over a long stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the one word serves as applause, a farewell and a thank-you in everyday British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Each phrase names one colloquial use of the same word: applause, a farewell, and thanks.

clue.text: Sounded delighted school has nothing to hide

indicators.note: to hide means the school word conceals the next piece inside it

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone made happy noises at a school with nothing to conceal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make soft dove-like murmurs, as one does when charmed or delighted by a baby.

clue.text: More time divorcee needed to get over stress

indicators.note: in a down clue, to get over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, such as a divorcee
tension means stress or strain

explanation.surface: A divorcee needs more time to get over the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get over' looks like recovering, but in a down clue it puts EX above TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is extra time allowed, as for a deadline or a loan.

clue.text: Scotch all the rage following game

indicators.note: following means the fashionable word comes after the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
in means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: Scotch whisky became fashionable after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it is the verb meaning to thwart or put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to wreck it or put an end to it.

clue.text: Sister to possibly a poet and painter

definitions.text: Sister to possibly a poet and painter

parts.words: Sister to possibly a poet and painter
parts.note: Christina, the Victorian poet, was sister to Dante Gabriel, who was both poet and painter; the surname covers both

explanation.walkthrough: The family name fits the poet Christina, the sister, and also her brother Dante Gabriel, the Pre-Raphaelite painter and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian family of that surname included the poet Christina and her brother, a Pre-Raphaelite painter who also wrote verse.

clue.text: Gloomy note found in safe after he died

indicators.note: after means these letters follow the abbreviation for he died

parts.note: OB is short for obiit, Latin for he died, seen on gravestones

indicators.note: found in means the note sits inside the word for safe

parts.note: sure means safe or certain, as in a sure bet
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A dark message turned up in a strongbox after the owner's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like a strongbox, but it means sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure can mean dark and dim, lacking light, so gloomy.

clue.text: Babies left in misery

parts.note: to baby someone is to coddle or spoil them
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Infants left in a wretched state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babies' is a verb, meaning spoils; 'misery' is a person, a killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a misery is a gloomy killjoy who stops others enjoying themselves.

clue.text: A tart picked up in US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: slut is a derogatory term synonymous with tart

explanation.surface: A loose woman is collected in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a pickup in a bar, but it reverses A SLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil city in Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: Assuming nothing new slipped into one article by expert

indicators.note: slipped into means the letter for new is put inside the next pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the is the definite article
a buff is an enthusiast and expert, as in a film buff

explanation.surface: Someone assumes nothing, while a new item gets into an expert's article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming nothing' means putting on no clothes, not taking nothing for granted; 'slipped into' puts N straight after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial idiom for naked, wearing no clothes, which is putting on nothing.

clue.text: Put right song at end of right record

indicators.note: at end of means the song comes after the other pieces

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Fixing a song placed at the end of the right record.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to mend or fix, which is to put right what was broken.

clue.text: Summarise unpopular course

parts.note: out of favour or out of fashion, so out
a line is a course or route taken, as in a line of action

explanation.surface: An instruction to sum up a course that nobody likes.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the main points in brief is to sketch them, a synonym for summing up.

clue.text: Drew attention to best returns available in rent

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the word for rent

parts.note: a rent is a tear or slit in cloth

indicators.note: returns means the word for best is read backwards

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Someone highlighted the best rental yields on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for a home, but here it is a tear; 'returns' turns the word for best round.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine a spotlight on something is, figuratively, to draw attention to it; the past tense matches drew.

clue.text: Refuse collected from outskirts of Dodge City?

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: NY stands for New York, the city par excellence

explanation.surface: Rubbish gathered from the edges of a Wild West town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a noun meaning rubbish, but it is the verb. The question mark flags NY as one example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse a request is to turn it down, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Paint, perhaps, learned person gripping a pen

indicators.note: gripping means the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a mage is a wise or learned man, a magus
a quill is a pen made from a feather

explanation.surface: A scholar holding a pen, with paint in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like a decorator's job, but here it is face paint, an example of make-up, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word for make-up covers face paint, so paint is an example of it, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Man on board, possibly sad case

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed
a jacket is a case or outer cover, as of a book or record

explanation.surface: A man on a ship, possibly depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means aboard ship, not on a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a sailor in the navy, from the blue jacket of the uniform.

clue.text: Spoiled lake with water rig? It's plain to see

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An oil rig has polluted a lake, and the damage is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shown on a grand scale is obvious, so the phrase means clear and evident to anyone.

clue.text: Determination shown with lower lip trembling?

indicators.note: trembling means the letters shake about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Strength of will shown despite a quivering lower lip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a trembling lip usually shows the opposite of resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is strength of will, the resolve that keeps one going.

clue.text: A sauce sent back with posh dish

indicators.note: sent back means the first two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: sauce means cheek or impudence, as does lip
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone returns a sauce served with an upmarket meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns A LIP into PILA. 'Sauce' looks culinary, but it is cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish cooked in stock with spices, also spelt pilaf; a dish by any name.

clue.text: Noted chap with the blues is to head corporation

parts.note: to head is to lead
corporation is old slang for a large belly

explanation.surface: A famous depressed man is going to run a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the blues' looks like sad, but he was an American blues and folk singer; 'corporation' means a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Huddie Ledbetter, the American folk and blues musician, performed under this stage name.

clue.text: Large one knight carried?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

indicators.note: carried means the knight is held inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Wondering about a big item a knight bore into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the weapon: a large thing that a knight carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear was the mounted knight's weapon at tournaments, which fits the whole clue as a description.

clue.text: Queen choked by poor health of partner

indicators.note: choked by means the queen is held tightly inside the rearranged letters
poor means the letters are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen whose partner's ill health weighs on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges two clue words as they are printed, and R, from Regina, lands inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for one's spouse or partner, the other half of a couple.

clue.text: Keys used for overtures?

definitions.meaning: keys are things that open locks
overtures are opening pieces or approaches, first moves

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers devices that open things, such as keys, and opening moves, such as overtures.

clue.text: Way rhymes sounded in golden age

indicators.note: sounded means the rhyming words are spoken aloud

parts.note: two words that rhyme with way, such as hay and day, said one after the other

explanation.surface: Rhymes for way were recited in a golden age.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words rhyming with 'way', hay and day, when spoken give the word for a golden age.
explanation.definitionFit: A time of greatest success or vigour is a prime or peak, a golden age.

clue.text: Magazine in Independent and Observer?

parts.note: private means independent, not state-run, as in a private school
an eye is something that observes

explanation.surface: Looking for a magazine inside two British newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent and The Observer are British newspapers, which makes the clue look like a media story. The answer is Britain's satirical fortnightly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's best-known satirical magazine bears this name, which also means a detective.

clue.text: Island with little business in capital after uprising

indicators.note: in means the business word goes inside the reversed piece
in a down clue, after uprising means the word for capital is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: A1 means capital, first-rate, written AI with 1 as I
biz is a short, informal word for business

explanation.surface: An island whose small firms operate in the capital after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, so capital; written with I for 1 and turned upwards by 'after uprising', it gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish island in the Balearics, famous for its nightlife.

clue.text: Lobbyists regularly passing notice

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Lobbyists keep coming by, and someone takes note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' means a death, not walking by.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of obituary, the notice published when someone has died, or passed away.

clue.text: Irish MP conserving small flower

indicators.note: conserving means the MP's letters keep the next piece inside them

parts.note: TD stands for Teachta Dala, a member of the Irish parliament
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: An Irish politician preserving a little flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, something that flows; this one runs along the border between Scotland and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river; this one runs through the Scottish Borders.

clue.text: Drug addict presumably stopped for a lift

definitions.text: Drug addict presumably stopped for a lift

parts.words: Drug addict presumably stopped for a lift
parts.note: a lift is a high from drugs, and an addict seeks one; the surface pictures a hitchhiker

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hitchhiker; 'lift' is the boost a drug gives its taker.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for someone who takes drugs, especially an addict.

clue.text: Minor difficulty in clever innovation

definitions.meaning: a small snag or problem to iron out
a neat new trick or technique, as in a new twist on an idea

explanation.surface: A small problem turns up in an ingenious new idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small snag and a clever trick or new method.

clue.text: Two answers about Beatles' first release

indicators.note: about means the two answer words surround the next letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
to solve is to answer a problem or clue

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word Beatles

explanation.surface: A Beatles debut record, praised with two answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like a record coming out, but it means set free. A and SOLVE go round the B of Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or guilt, so it means to release.

clue.text: Sort date out? This may confirm running order

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fix a date; this check may confirm the vehicle runs properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running order' looks like a programme schedule, but it means a car being in working order.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial drive of a vehicle confirms that it is roadworthy and runs properly.

clue.text: Battle left couple of editors in tatters

parts.note: a fray is a fight or battle

indicators.note: a couple of means the first two letters of the word editors

explanation.surface: After a fight two editors were left with their clothes torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth that has worn ragged at the edges is torn and in shreds, so in tatters.
